pairs.title: fix(monomorph): resolve cross-module generic function return types

verdict.defect: When a generic function from another module was called, its return type was resolved without the function's type parameters in scope, and the monomorphized call kept the original module source, so the call was resolved and typed incorrectly.
verdict.reason: The culprit only refactored lookup_function_return_type to clone the return-type AST, and its lower.rs change only adds ForOf handling. Generics and the monomorphizer don't appear in its diff, so the type-parameter scoping gap came from later generic support and couldn't be seen in this diff.

pairs.title: fix: resolve struct naming conflicts across modules

verdict.defect: The new `struct_name_index` in `TypeTable` is keyed only by struct name, so same-named structs from different modules overwrite each other and `find_struct_by_name` can return the wrong module's struct.
verdict.reason: The culprit replaced the plain-struct fallback loop, which explicitly checked `struct_source == &module_source`, with a name-only O(1) index lookup; the removed module check is visible in the diff. The fix re-keys the index by (name, module_source); its namespace-import resolver additions are partly feature work, but the core regression comes from the culprit.

pairs.title: fix: enable SQLite parser with backtracking and channel(HIDDEN) support

verdict.defect: The parser generator emitted parsers that could not handle grammars like SQLite: left-recursive alternatives recursed into themselves forever, and group alternatives with overlapping FIRST sets became unreachable `else if` branches.
verdict.reason: The culprit introduced `gen_parse_fn`, `gen_multi_alt_body` and `gen_consume_group`, which dispatch on FIRST sets alone with no backtracking or left-recursion handling; that is exactly what the fix replaces. A reviewer could see that left recursion was ignored and that `gen_consume_group` emits duplicate conditions when alternatives share FIRST tokens, though much of the fix reads as new backtracking functionality.

pairs.title: fix: resolve gale parser bugs and variant-in-variant codegen ICE

verdict.defect: The match-ergonomics boxing check skipped boxing whenever the payload field was any ref type, even when the binding expected a Box<Inner> and the payload was ref Inner, as with variant-in-variant payloads. This produced mismatched ref types and a codegen crash.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the `needs_boxing` predicate that treats every `WirType::Ref` payload as not needing boxing without comparing type ids. The fix replaces exactly this predicate with a type-id comparison. The flawed coarse check is plainly visible in the culprit's added lines, though spotting it needs an understanding of how variant payloads are lowered.

pairs.title: fix(resolver): bind trait type params to impl args in default methods

verdict.defect: When a default method of a generic trait (e.g. `trait Maker<T>`) was synthesized for or looked up on an impl, the trait's type parameters were never bound to the impl's concrete trait arguments. `T` inside the body or signature therefore stayed unresolved, producing wrong types or `T^Trait::method` calls that never got monomorphized.
verdict.reason: The culprit added both default-method synthesis in the impl loop and default-method lookup in method resolution. In both places it calls `resolve_method`/`resolve_type` on the trait's default method without binding the trait's own generic params to the impl's trait args, and the fix patches exactly those sites. A reviewer could ask how `T` in `trait Foo<T>` default bodies resolves, since the diff only passes the trait name and the impl type.

pairs.title: fix(resolver): cross-module aliased generic type inference + CalleeRef refactor

verdict.defect: Calls to an aliased cross-module generic function without turbofish failed type inference. `lookup_generic_func_for_inference` re-looked up the symbol table by the defining-module name, but the table is keyed by the local alias.
verdict.reason: The culprit is a pure refactor that moved existing call-resolution code into submodules. The faulty `infer_fn_type_args` / `lookup_generic_func_for_inference` path does not appear in its diff at all; blame lands on the callee-tuple code that was only relocated there.

pairs.title: fix(cli/doc): recognise fenced code blocks in render_md_doc

verdict.defect: render_md_doc in wado-cli/src/doc.rs did not recognise fenced code blocks, so `#` lines were treated as headings and alignment whitespace inside the code was collapsed.
verdict.reason: The bug lives in the doc renderer, which the culprit never touched. The culprit only edited serde.wado doc comments, which the fix rewrote as content, so blame points at the wrong PR.

pairs.title: fix(opt): enumerate WithHandler / Resume / TemplateString in catch-all walkers

verdict.defect: No wrong behaviour is corrected: the fix swaps catch-all `_` arms and silent no-op arms for explicit variant lists and `unreachable!` assertions on TemplateString/WithHandler/Resume, variants that by the fix's own messages never reach these phases.
verdict.reason: This is a defensive exhaustiveness refactor that adds assertions for variants already eliminated earlier, so no observable bug is fixed. The culprit's `strip_in_expr` treating those variants as no-ops is consistent with that invariant, not a defect.

pairs.title: fix(closure): contextual types, stable functor IDs, scope hygiene

verdict.defect: Closure lowering had three faults: it matched Closure nodes to functors with a counter re-walked in lockstep across passes, it never lowered nested closures inside generated `__call` bodies, and it let pattern-lowering temps and local maps in closure bodies use the outer function's local-index namespace; together these caused mis-matched functors and colliding locals (invalid Wasm).
verdict.reason: The fix addresses real miscompilations, including nested closure literals failing Wasm validation and pattern temps colliding with closure params. The culprit is an 'extract' refactor that created `closure.rs` and `pattern.rs` wholesale by moving existing logic from elsewhere, so blame lands on moved code rather than code it introduced, and nothing in a pure move would draw a reviewer to these latent issues.

pairs.title: fix(lsp): clean diagnostics when opening bundled stdlib files

verdict.defect: Opening a bundled stdlib file in the LSP produced spurious errors: prelude-collision errors against the types the file itself defines, duplicate-definition errors from an entry copy and a cached copy of the same module, and occasional codegen panics.
verdict.reason: The root causes are in the compiler: `check_prelude_collisions` keyed off `is_core()` rather than `#![no_prelude]`, and the loader gave stdlib entry files an EntryPoint identity instead of their canonical identity. The culprit only wrote the LSP glue that calls `compile_with_options`, and nothing in that diff shows the stdlib-entry identity or collision problem.

pairs.title: fix(cm_binding): address #997 follow-up bugs from #996 review

verdict.defect: List lift/lower used the non-registry `cm_abi::cm_size`/`cm_align` (4-byte i32-handle fallback) as the element stride for named WASI types, flat-result lifting used `TypeTable::I32` placeholders, stream CM names were mechanically kebab-cased, and non-Result task-return emitted a hard-coded `task-return(0)`.
verdict.reason: The culprit is a pure refactor that moved this code verbatim out of the 10K-line cm_binding.rs into submodules. Every defective line already existed in the removed original, so the culprit did not introduce any of the wrong behaviour.

pairs.title: fix(gale): close 3 ANTLR4 stage_b compatibility gaps

verdict.defect: Generated LR loops committed to a left-recursive suffix on first-token match alone, so a suffix that failed partway made the whole parse fail or left `p.pos` mid-suffix. Separately, list-label (`+=`) LR alts produced type-mismatched struct literals, and keyword-shaped lexer rules with no carrier rule were unreachable.
verdict.reason: The culprit only wrapped the pre-existing direct suffix call (`result = suffix_fn(p, result, start)?`) in a precedence check; the first-token-only commit already existed before it. The scan-side loop, the list-label handling and the keyword classification are not in the culprit's diff at all.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): hash generator sources via canonical token stream

verdict.defect: Generator source hashes were computed over raw file bytes, so comment, docstring and whitespace edits to .wado files changed generator_source_hash; this is a policy choice rather than incorrect behaviour.
verdict.reason: The fix swaps the hashing policy to a canonical token stream so cosmetic edits are ignored, which is an enhancement: byte hashing was deterministic, and the determinism and revert tests would pass with it too. The culprit's byte-content hash worked as designed, so there is no defect for a reviewer to spot.

pairs.title: fix(dev-tools): surface buffered diagnostics on empty golden output

verdict.defect: When a compile failed or produced no phase output, the golden-fixture tool reported only a generic 'compilation failed' or 'Empty output' message and dropped the diagnostics the silent host had buffered.
verdict.reason: The tool already failed loudly in these cases and still fails the same way; the fix only adds the buffered error diagnostics to the message, a debuggability improvement rather than a correction of wrong behaviour. The culprit did write the context-dropping `map_err` and `if let Some` code, but since there is no defect to attribute, neither 'introduced' nor 'visible' applies.

pairs.title: fix(lower): reject Binding default in dense-int Switch rewrite

verdict.defect: The dense-integer Switch rewrite accepted a `Binding` pattern as the default arm, but `build` never emitted a `Let` binding the local to the scrutinee, so the bound variable silently read as zero.
verdict.reason: The fix's own comment says the same gap existed before 9.C.1, and the culprit is a refactor that relocated the existing Switch analysis and build code into the translator rather than writing the bug. The defect is still readable in the culprit's diff: `analyze` accepts `Wildcard | Binding`, and `build` only clones the arm body with no binding.

pairs.title: fix(tagpr): sync Cargo.lock via postVersionCommand to fix --locked CI

verdict.defect: The .tagpr config ran `cargo update --workspace` under the wrong key (`command`, which runs before the version bump) and placed it outside any `[tagpr]` section, so it was ignored or a no-op. Cargo.lock stayed stale in release PRs and `cargo --locked` CI broke.
verdict.reason: The culprit created .tagpr with bare, sectionless git-config keys and used `command` instead of `postVersionCommand`; the fix moves the keys under `[tagpr]` and switches to `postVersionCommand`. A reviewer who knows git-config format could see the missing section header, though spotting the wrong key needs tagpr knowledge.

pairs.title: fix: unify break value types in labeled block expressions

verdict.defect: Labeled block expressions took the type of the first `break` value without unifying or checking the others, and ignored the use-site expected type, so mismatched break types went undiagnosed and literals did not coerce.
verdict.reason: The culprit is a refactor that split the resolver into new submodule files, carrying over the existing `break_types[0]` logic with its TODO comment. It moved the defect rather than introducing it, although the TODO makes the gap visible in its diff.

pairs.title: fix: address review feedback on labeled block break unification

verdict.defect: `patch_unresolved_null` rewrote a bare `null` to whatever result type a sibling branch or arm chose, even a non-Option type like `i32`, so `if c { null } else { 42 }` (and the match equivalent) was silently accepted and produced ill-typed TIR that crashed WIR translation.
verdict.reason: The culprit added both the 'defer UNKNOWN to the sibling type' selection in if/match and the unconditional `expr.type_id = target_type` rewrite, and that rewrite visibly lacks any check that the target is an Option. The labeled-block and shadowed-label parts of the fix concern code the culprit did not write.

pairs.title: fix(serve): bound the response body pump with an idle timeout

verdict.defect: A client that stops draining the response body but keeps the connection open makes the body pump's `frame_tx.send` block forever, pinning the handler task's fiber stack indefinitely.
verdict.reason: The culprit removed the wall-clock `tokio::time::timeout` around `run_concurrent`, whose deleted comment named exactly this non-draining-client case, and left the per-request pump with no bound on `frame_tx.send`. The deletion and its explanatory comment are both visible in the diff.

pairs.title: fix: run the epoch ticker on a dedicated OS thread

verdict.defect: The epoch ticker ran as a tokio task, so a runaway guest in pure wasm that blocked the only tokio worker thread (single-core host) starved the ticker; the epoch never advanced and the server deadlocked.
verdict.reason: The culprit moved guest execution onto long-lived worker tasks that rely solely on the epoch deadline to trap runaways, yet kept the ticker as a tokio task. Its own doc comments say the guest monopolises the thread, so a reviewer could see the ticker could be starved.

pairs.title: fix: create tagpr release as draft so release.yml can upload assets

verdict.defect: tagpr created a published GitHub Release on tagging, and because the repository has Immutable releases enabled, release.yml's action-gh-release step could not upload build assets to it.
verdict.reason: The culprit set up the tagpr config and the release workflow without making the release a draft, so the upload failed; the fix adds `release = draft`. Whether that breaks depends on the repository's Immutable releases setting, which isn't in the diff, so a reviewer reading only the diff couldn't reasonably have caught it (beyond perhaps noticing the odd `release = patch` value).

pairs.title: fix(resolver): enforce fn mut root-mutability for non-identifier callees

verdict.defect: The `fn mut` FnMut rule (callee binding must be `mut`) was enforced only for plain identifier callees, so calls through non-`mut` roots like `(h.f)()` or `arr[0]()` compiled without the required diagnostic.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the ClosureMutBindingRequired check, but only inside the identifier-local branch, leaving the indirect-call path for field and index callees unchecked. A reviewer could see that the new rule applied to only one callee shape.

pairs.title: fix(optimize): field_scalarize must not propagate post-sync state past a labeled break (#1187)

verdict.defect: The dataflow walker took the fall-through state as the post-state of a labeled block and ignored labeled `break`s, which emit no sync. When an early exit (such as an inlined early return) skipped a sync inside the block, later code trusted a stale scalar and dropped field writes.
verdict.reason: The culprit's `walk_stmt` LabeledBlock arm only calls `walk_block` and uses the linear exit state, and its Break arm explicitly leaves labeled breaks uncommitted. Its own comment admits the walker "can't precisely model the post-block JOIN", so a reviewer could flag that labeled-break exit states never reach the post-block state.

pairs.title: fix(optimize): address branch-review findings in NIR mod_ref / sroa_param / elide_box_local

verdict.defect: `can_move_past` checked `may_clobber` in one direction only (whether the intervening statement clobbers the moved expression), so an inner initializer that calls code writing a global could be moved past a sibling that reads that global, giving wrong results.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the WIR `can_move_past` ending in `!int_mr.may_clobber(expr_mr)` and wired it into adjacent struct elision. The fix replaces it with a check in both directions and adds a regression fixture for exactly this reordering. The one-sided check and its doc comment (condition 4) are plainly visible in the culprit diff.

pairs.title: fix(gale): stamp min_prec / variant_id on LR self-refs nested in containers

verdict.defect: Self-recursive calls nested inside Repeat/Group/OptionalLookahead in an LR suffix kept the default min_prec=0 and lacked the variant id, so e.g. `(',' b+=expr)*` consumed the outer `'>>'` and parsing stopped at the first comma.
verdict.reason: The parse-side `stamp_lr_self_ref_min_prec` was already top-level-only before the culprit, and nested scan calls already used the default 0; the culprit only carried that same shallow walk over to the scan side. The affected tests were long-standing TODOs, so the gap predates the culprit rather than being introduced by it.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): demote per-file regeneration notice to debug

verdict.defect: The per-file 'regenerating' diagnostic was emitted at Warning severity, which produced noisy output when a generator edit regenerated hundreds of files.
verdict.reason: The fix only lowers a diagnostic's severity from Warning to Debug as a noise-reduction policy change; nothing crashed or computed a wrong result. The culprit's Warning level was a deliberate, documented design choice rather than a bug.

pairs.title: fix(zlib): decode gzip FNAME/FCOMMENT as UTF-8

verdict.defect: `bytes_to_string` turned each gzip FNAME/FCOMMENT byte into its own char (Latin-1 style), while `gzip_compress_with_header` writes the names' UTF-8 bytes, so non-ASCII names and comments came back garbled.
verdict.reason: The culprit added both the UTF-8 byte writer (`get_byte`) and the byte-as-char reader `bytes_to_string`, so the round-trip mismatch starts there. A reviewer could spot it by comparing the two functions in the same diff.

pairs.title: fix(synthesis): cm_binding boundary bug fixes + migrate walkers to TirVisitor

verdict.defect: Signed i8/i16 CM values were lifted with zero-extending loads, so -1 became 255/65535. Separately, the record stream-read discovery walker did not descend into if-expressions and other containers, leaving the rewriter to call a binding function that was never synthesized.
verdict.reason: The culprit PR is a pure file-split refactor (cm_binding.rs into submodules). It moved the already-existing i32_load8_u/i16 lift code and the partial walkers verbatim into new files, so it did not introduce the defects; blame just lands on the new files.

pairs.title: fix(gale): two Stage A lexer bugs (EOF-suffix rule priority, channel tokens)

verdict.defect: The keyword-classifier shortcut admitted a keyword candidate even when a colliding carrier rule was declared before it, so a carrier match (e.g. `A : 'a' EOF;`) was re-tagged as the later keyword rule (`B : 'a';`), breaking ANTLR4's first-rule priority; separately, `to_lexer_string` dropped non-default-channel tokens.
verdict.reason: Before the culprit, every keyword candidate was classified as a keyword unconditionally, so the mis-tagging already existed; the culprit only added a reachability filter, which the fix rewrote, and it did not create the priority bug. The channel-token bug is in `runtime.wado`, which the culprit never touched.

pairs.title: fix(hooks): reconcile vendor/wasmtime to pinned commit every session

verdict.defect: The setup hook only ran `git submodule update` when vendor/wasmtime/Cargo.toml was absent, so a checkout that was already populated but at the wrong commit was never reset to the pinned gitlink SHA, and builds ran against a drifting wasmtime.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the `[ ! -f vendor/wasmtime/Cargo.toml ]` guard that skips reconciliation whenever the checkout exists. A reviewer could ask what happens if the submodule is present at the wrong commit, though knowing the container provisions it at the branch tip helps.

pairs.title: fix(jco): run example/hello.wado on upstream jco b1f93c27

verdict.defect: No defect in the culprit: the shim's synchronous `{tag: "ok"}` return and the build/patch setup no longer matched the behaviour of a newer upstream jco checkout (async results lowered as futures, pnpm workspace, automatic WASI shim rewriting).
verdict.reason: The fix bumps vendor/jco to a new upstream commit and adapts the shim, build script and rebased patch to it, which is a dependency upgrade rather than a correction of wrong behaviour. The culprit's code was correct for the jco version it pinned, so a reviewer could not have flagged it.

pairs.title: fix(benchmark): fixed header/legend/axis on combined benchmark pages

verdict.defect: No real defect: the chart title, legend and y-axis scrolled out of view with the horizontally scrolling chart, and the change pins them and adds a new wasm-size page.
verdict.reason: This is a UI enhancement plus a new feature page, not a fix for wrong behaviour. The horizontal scroller it adjusts was added by a later change, not by the culprit, whose page had no scrolling at all.

pairs.title: fix(benchmark): render wasm-size graphs and serialize gh-pages writes

verdict.defect: The new wasm-size page skipped every benchmark name without a ` (-Ox)` suffix, and wasm-size programs never carry one, so the page drew no graphs.
verdict.reason: The culprit created wasm-size-index.html with grouping logic that explicitly drops unsuffixed names (the comment 'Skip entries without optimization level suffix'). A reviewer who knew the wasm-size bench names had no -O suffix could have flagged that it renders nothing; the concurrency part of the fix is a separate, pre-existing workflow race.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): attribute method-signature use→def edges to the owning module

verdict.defect: Method-info lookup resolved a foreign impl/resource method's signature types and recorded those use→def edges keyed under the consumer module. AstId collisions then clobbered real edges in the consumer, so liveness dropped a reachable function and the compiler crashed with an unresolved call.
verdict.reason: The culprit only moved the references map from a shared Rc<RefCell> into per-module ModuleSemantics. The use key was already built from current_module_source with the foreign AstId before that change, so the mis-keying predates it and nothing in its diff reveals the collision.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): infer trailing type params on a partial turbofish

verdict.defect: When a call gave only some explicit type arguments (a partial turbofish), type-argument inference was skipped entirely, so the trailing type params stayed unsubstituted and either caused a spurious type mismatch or a codegen panic.
verdict.reason: The culprit diff shown is empty, and its topic (associated type bounds in blanket impl method resolution) is unrelated to skipping inference on a partial turbofish. Blame likely landed on the culprit only because it touched or reformatted the surrounding `if type_args.is_empty()` lines.

pairs.title: fix(wir): guard representation-crossing casts; perf: IEEE bit assembly for wide-int float conversions

verdict.defect: No wrong behaviour is corrected: the culprit's power-of-two scaling loops in u128::as_f64/as_f32 already gave correctly rounded results, including infinity saturation, and the WIR change only adds an assertion.
verdict.reason: The int128.wado change is a performance rewrite that swaps the exact scaling loops for direct IEEE bit assembly with identical results. The wir.rs/primitive_ops.rs change is a defensive assert that makes an earlier lowering gap fail loudly, rather than fixing a bug in the blamed culprit lines.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): dispatch concrete-generic trait impls to the correct module

verdict.defect: Concrete impls on a generic head (`impl Tag for List<Token>`) were indexed and dispatched under the unqualified argument spelling (`List<Token>`), so same-named argument types from different modules collided and a generic-bound call could be routed to the wrong module's impl.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `instantiated_type_name` (AST simple names) and `simplify_generic_type_args` (strips module qualifiers) as the lookup bridge, which by design erases the module distinction. The fix removes both and keys on the qualified resolved name. Stripping qualifiers to match a key is a visibly lossy design that a careful reviewer could flag as collision-prone.

pairs.title: fix(cm): make all wasi:cli/exit functions work

verdict.defect: Calling the stable `wasi:cli/exit#exit` (and so `exit_success`/`exit_error`) crashed the compiler, because CM lowering of a `Result<(), ()>` argument was missing and effect-operation parameter types were not used for inference.
verdict.reason: The culprit only added TODO comments documenting the existing compiler crash and enabled the exit-with-code link option. It did not write the missing lowering logic or the `Exit::exit(Ok(()))` calls, which already existed before it.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): don't double-stamp the generated header

verdict.defect: The Kiln driver always prepended its canonical `#![generated]` header to every generator output, so a generator that stamps its own header (like Gale) got two headers, with the driver's `by` overriding the generator's.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the unconditional header-prepend loop in `execute`, which the fix makes conditional on `has_generated_marker`. Spotting the problem would have required anticipating generators that self-stamp, a use case not present in the culprit, which documents unconditional stamping as intended design.

pairs.title: fix(cli): share Kiln generator AOT cache across a `wado test` run

verdict.defect: Each per-fixture host in a `wado test` run had its own Kiln component cache, so a shared generator was AOT-compiled once per fixture instead of once per run (slow but correct).
verdict.reason: The fix lifts the per-host component cache into a shared `KilnComponentCache` threaded through `wado test`; this is a performance optimisation, not a correction of wrong output, a crash or a hang. The culprit's per-host cache worked as designed and introduced no incorrect behaviour, only a narrower cache scope.

pairs.title: fix(cm): fix Future<Result<(), ErrorCode>> read ICE and unify future-read on the shared CM lift
fix: keep cross-module fn-param closure specializations distinct

verdict.defect: Closure fn-param specialization looked up callees and keyed specializations by bare function name, so same-named functions in different modules (e.g. two `run_entry`s) were conflated, leaking one module's types into the other and producing invalid Wasm.
verdict.reason: The culprit is a visitor-port refactor that only carried over the existing name-only `func_by_name` map and `FnParamSpecKey { callee_name, .. }`; the removed code already keyed on `func.name` alone. A reviewer could still spot the unqualified key in the rewritten lines, but the culprit did not introduce it.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): resolve inline-clause paths relative to the declaring file

verdict.defect: Inline Kiln `from`/`inputs`/`output_dir` paths were used as written rather than resolved relative to the declaring .wado file, so sibling consumers with the same `./grammar.g4` read the wrong schema or wrote to colliding output dirs, and malformed-clause diagnostics were silently dropped.
verdict.reason: The faulty path lowering (`InvocationPath::normalize(&use_decl.source)` in kiln/inline.rs) and the `unwrap_or_default()` that swallowed errors predate the culprit. The culprit's blamed lines are example files whose explicit `output_dir` values are correct workarounds under the old semantics, plus the transitive-harvest plumbing, which only widened exposure to the bug.

pairs.title: fix: canonicalize local module identity so each file loads once

verdict.defect: A module reachable through more than one relative import path (a diamond, or a `../` escape that re-enters the entry dir) got path-dependent, non-canonical loader identities, so the culprit's harvest-key→loader-identity map recorded only the first-visited spelling and the Kiln redirect missed (or was silently overwritten last-write-wins) for the other spelling.
verdict.reason: The loader's non-canonical relative composition predates the culprit, but the culprit added the cross-module Kiln harvest. That harvest assumes one loader identity per file and remaps the index with silent last-write-wins, which breaks redirects on alternate import paths. Its own doc comment describes the per-path identity derivation, so a reviewer could have asked what happens when a module is reached two ways.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): treat `pub` as a liveness root, like `export`

verdict.defect: The liveness pass did not seed `pub` functions and globals as production roots, so public library API items with no in-package caller were falsely reported as `DeadFunction` / `DeadGlobal`.
verdict.reason: The culprit created `liveness.rs`, whose root condition (`func.is_export || has_export_attr || world_export_names`) leaves out `pub`, and it never seeds globals at all. A reviewer could see that the 'package-external boundary' roots omit `pub` visibility, so public API items would be flagged as dead.

pairs.title: fix(benchmark): order runtime graphs by latest run, retire legacy json/* series

verdict.defect: Graphs were ordered by first appearance in the historical data, and benchmark series no longer emitted (the legacy suffix-less json/* names) were still drawn.
verdict.reason: The fix is a presentation change: it reorders graphs to follow the latest run and hides series retired by later benchmark renames. Nothing was crashing or computing a wrong result. The culprit's first-appearance ordering was a reasonable choice when it was written; it only looked stale after later benchmark changes.

pairs.title: fix(vscode): restore extension name `wado`

verdict.defect: The culprit renamed the package `name` from `wado` to `wado-vscode`, which changes the VS Code extension identifier (`wado-lang.wado` becomes `wado-lang.wado-vscode`) and breaks the extension's identity.
verdict.reason: The fix reverts exactly the `name` lines the culprit changed in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The unintended rename sits plainly in what was supposed to be a dependency-update chore PR, so a reviewer could have flagged it.

pairs.title: fix(publish): unblock releasing facade/types-only libraries; export marl escape helpers

verdict.defect: The compiler rejected `--lib` builds of types-only (data-model) libraries as 'exports nothing', and marl's escape helpers were `pub` rather than `export`; together these broke publishing those packages.
verdict.reason: The real defects sit in the compiler's empty-export check and marl's `html.wado`, neither of which the culprit touched. The culprit's `publish.rs` lines were changed only to make `--dry-run` also build, a deliberate behaviour change to the documented check-only dry run, not a correction of a bug the culprit introduced.

pairs.title: fix(gale): don't over-shadow a named single-literal lexer rule

verdict.defect: The gale lexer generator replaced a named single-literal rule (e.g. `LBRACE: '{' -> pushMode`) with an inline literal matcher that used default extras, so the rule's lexer commands were dropped; it also deduplicated literal rules defined in non-default modes, leaving those modes without a matcher.
verdict.reason: The bug lives in package-gale/src/lexer_gen.wado, which the culprit never touched. The culprit only edited the example Wado.g4 grammar, using OPEN_BRACE/CLOSE_BRACE named tokens that worked around the generator bug, and the fix reverts that grammar back to inline braces. Blame landed on the grammar lines, not on the code that caused the defect.

pairs.title: fix(cli): make dependency-cache write_atomic concurrency-safe

verdict.defect: write_atomic named its temp file only by process id, so concurrent threads in one process writing the same path shared a temp file, and one thread's rename could move it away before another's rename, which then failed.
verdict.reason: The culprit added write_atomic with the pid-only temp name, and its own comment says it only guards against concurrent writers in different processes. A reviewer could see that writers on separate threads within one process collide.

pairs.title: fix(format): preserve doc comments on trait associated types

verdict.defect: The formatter (unparse.rs) dropped leading doc comments on trait associated-type declarations and mishandled blank lines before attributed trait methods, so comments were lost and the output was not idempotent.
verdict.reason: The bug lives in unparse.rs, which the culprit never touched. The culprit only added a new Reflect trait to traits.wado, whose stray double blank lines are a symptom of the existing formatter bug rather than its cause.

pairs.title: fix(elaborator): once-eval compound assignment (#1179) and non-primitive index-key coercion (#1628)

verdict.defect: A compound assignment like `arr[bump()] += 1` evaluated impure target sub-expressions (subscripts, owned bases) twice, once for the read and once for the write, and list-literal subscripts were not coerced to a non-primitive Index key type.
verdict.reason: Issue #1179 predates the culprit, and the original elaborator already emitted the target twice, so the culprit's new reify.rs ported existing double-evaluation behaviour rather than introducing it. The key-coercion half lives in method_lookup/expr.rs, which the culprit did not touch. The duplicated `reify_expr(&compound.target)` walk is plainly visible in the culprit's code, and its own comment says it walks the AST twice.

pairs.title: fix(cargo-cache): make the web container reuse CI's sccache compile cache

verdict.defect: The CI job and the container's warm-cache build ran with different CARGO_* environment variables, and sccache hashes every CARGO_* var into its cache key. As a result every container lookup missed CI's cache.
verdict.reason: The culprit added both the runner env block (CARGO_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, CARGO_INCREMENTAL) and the warm-cache command, which sets only CARGO_INCREMENTAL and inherits whatever else the container has. A reviewer familiar with sccache key inputs could spot the env mismatch between the two sides.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): remove superlinear value-graph invalidation churn (Gale O3 OOM)

verdict.defect: The value-graph builder minted a fresh opaque for every tracked local at every call, loop, guard and labeled-block invalidation, and recomputed nested block write sets without caching, so memory grew superlinearly and Gale ran out of memory at O3.
verdict.reason: The dominant churn is per-call invalidation over `mut_escaped` locals in `bump_call_effects`, which a later PR added; the culprit only contributed the uncached write-collection and per-loop opaque minting, which was harmless at its original scale. From the culprit's diff alone, a reviewer could not reasonably have predicted an OOM caused by code that did not yet exist.

pairs.title: fix(cm): skip a provider whose dependency was eliminated instead of panicking

verdict.defect: Composing a program with a provider whose dependency component had been dead-code-eliminated (so no dependency was instantiated) bailed with 'no composed dependency imports provider interface' and failed compilation, instead of skipping the unused provider.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the provider-wiring loop with the unconditional `bail!` when no dependency instance imports the interface. A reviewer could see that `dep_instances` only holds dependencies whose exports are in the import plan, while `providers` is not filtered the same way, so an empty match was reachable.

pairs.title: fix(gale): terminate scan on mandatory-group mismatch; reject hidden/indirect left recursion

verdict.defect: Mandatory multi-alt scan groups were emitted as `lenient`, so on a gate miss they matched zero tokens instead of failing. A rule whose required group's FIRST set is reachable through its own recursive tail then re-entered itself without consuming input and exhausted the stack.
verdict.reason: The culprit flipped `lenient: false` to `lenient: true` in `lower_general_scan_group` and `lower_simple_cst_scan_group`, and added the lenient gate/fall-through in `gen_scan_op_group`. That is exactly what the fix makes conditional on the rule being scan-cyclic. A reviewer could see that a required group now silently matches empty, which risks zero-consumption recursion in recursive-descent scans.

pairs.title: fix(cli): tolerate concurrent removal in kiln output reconcile

verdict.defect: walk_and_delete propagated NotFound errors from read_dir, entry iteration, file_type and remove_file. If another process removed a file or directory during reconcile, the whole pipeline failed with an I/O error.
verdict.reason: The culprit added walk_and_delete with bare `?` on every filesystem call, and the fix replaces exactly those calls with NotFound-tolerant matches. A reviewer could notice this TOCTOU fragility, especially since reconcile_outputs already handles a missing directory with an exists() check.

pairs.title: fix(gale): decide optionals in the op-only walker as the surface walker does

verdict.defect: The op-only walker's `gen_repeat_body` decided every `?` inside LR suffixes with a single one-token first-set check. It ignored the lowered Optional strategy (lookahead, scan guard, shape lookahead) and non-greedy `??`, so it entered optionals wrongly and mis-parsed or rejected input such as `SELECT a IN t`.
verdict.reason: The culprit replaced `gen_lr_suffix_helpers`, which routed suffix repeats through the strategy-aware `gen_op_repeat`, with the new `gen_ops`/`gen_repeat_body` walker whose Optional arm is a bare `if first_check`. A reviewer comparing it with `gen_op_storable_optional`'s strategy match in the same diff could see that `r.strategy` and `??` handling were dropped.

pairs.title: fix(cm): reclaim linear memory at the synchronously-lifted export boundary

verdict.defect: Synchronously-lifted `--lib` exports were emitted with no `post-return` canonical option and never freed caller-lowered string parameters, so every call leaked its return area and the payload and parameter buffers in linear memory.
verdict.reason: The culprit introduced the sync lift for library exports, building `lift_opts` without `Async` but also without any `PostReturn`, and its primitive set included `String`, which is returned through guest memory. A reviewer familiar with the Canonical ABI could flag that a sync lift returning memory-backed values needs `post-return` to reclaim them.

pairs.title: fix(cm): free the buffers a `task.return` payload owns

verdict.defect: An async export's `task.return` payload buffers (strings, lists and nested buffers lowered into flat slots) were never freed, leaking linear memory per call; separately, a `task return` value was not type-checked against the declared result.
verdict.reason: The culprit only added the sync `post-return` free walk in `cm_free.rs`; the fix refactors that walk and reuses it for the flat slots. The `task.return` leak predates the culprit, which explicitly documents it as the unfixed D2 (issue #1708), so the culprit's lines did not introduce it.

pairs.title: fix(optimizer): sroa_param must not snapshot a boxed reference parameter

verdict.defect: sroa_param treated a boxed `&T`/`&mut T` parameter (lowered to a by-value `Box<T>`) as a harmless copy, so it scalarized it into a call-time snapshot even when a sibling `&mut`, a by-value holder, a global or a closure could write the same box, and the write was lost.
verdict.reason: The `candidate_is_ref` early return that skips boxed (by-value) candidates already existed in the pre-culprit `param_may_alias_sibling`. The culprit broadened the alias checks for real reference params but kept that exemption, so the miscompile predates it. Still, the culprit's diff states both 'by-value candidate is already a copy' and that the pass unwraps the `Box<Scalar>` that `&T` params become, so a careful reviewer could have connected the two.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): output reconciliation spares a staging temp

verdict.defect: Kiln output reconciliation (walk_and_delete) treated a concurrent writer's in-flight write_atomic staging temp, which already carries the generated header, as an orphaned output and deleted it.
verdict.reason: The culprit only made the cache temp-file name unique per thread (pid plus counter). The bug comes from kiln_driver later publishing outputs through write_atomic while reconcile_outputs scans the same directory, and nothing in the culprit's cache-only diff shows that interaction.

pairs.title: fix(elaborator): let a trait-qualified call name a bound's implied supertraits

verdict.defect: Supertraits were tracked by their spelling in the declaring module and then re-resolved by that bare name in the caller's frame. As a result, a shadowing local trait, a `use ... as` alias, or a qualified call naming an implied supertrait resolved to the wrong declaration, wrongly reported ambiguity, or failed to resolve.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `elaborate_bound_names`, the name-keyed `push_unique_bound`/`SupertraitClosureIndex`, `bound_implies` and `supertraits_of`, all of which compare traits by name. The fix replaces that identity with declaration keys. A reviewer could see in the culprit's diff that inherited bound names, written in another module, are later looked up via `trait_declares_method` in the current frame.

pairs.title: fix(gale): a parser literal is an alias for the lexer rule it duplicates

verdict.defect: A parser inline literal whose text duplicated a whole single-literal lexer rule minted its own anonymous TK_LIT_* token and deduped the named rule away. This dropped the rule's action, made alternatives that reference the rule by name unreachable, and diverged from ANTLR4, where the literal is an alias for the rule.
verdict.reason: The literal-vs-rule dedup behaviour lives in the literal collection and lexer generation code, which predates the culprit. The culprit only added a highlight-side `shadow` workaround so name-based highlight mappings still fire, and the fix deletes that workaround once the root cause is addressed.

pairs.title: fix(cache): decide the target restore on cargo's lock, and bound incremental state

verdict.defect: The target restore skipped whenever target/ existed, so resumed containers whose image already had a target/ never got the cache restored. The staging-plus-rename approach could not merge into an existing tree.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the `existsSync(TARGET_DIR)` skip and the staging-plus-rename restore, and the fix replaces both. A reviewer could see that a pre-existing target/ (e.g. from an image snapshot) would permanently disable the restore, and that a rename fails onto a non-empty directory.

pairs.title: fix: stop the e2e suite failing tests for the machine's load

verdict.defect: Under machine load the e2e harness timed tests out by wall-clock epoch deadlines and on a shared single-core tokio runtime, and the guest subtask wait loop only stopped on payload == 2 (RETURNED), never on the CANCELLED states.
verdict.reason: The culprit only restructured where the HTTP response body is collected inside run_concurrent. It did not add the epoch deadline, the shared runtime or the payload == 2 check that the fix replaces. Blame lands there only because the fix touches neighbouring lines in e2e.rs.

pairs.title: fix(elaborator): classify `as` cast operands by their ultimate base type

verdict.defect: The new unrelated-aggregate cast check classified the source and target by their raw types rather than their ultimate base types, and it exempted any i128/u128 target, so some invalid casts compiled without a diagnostic: newtypes of aggregates, generic instances like List/ArraySlice, variants, and struct-to-wide-int.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the `unrelated_aggregate` block with `tt.get(source_type)`, `is_tuple` and a `!wide_int(target_type)` exemption, and the fix rewrites exactly that logic to use base types and cover more aggregate kinds. A reviewer could see that the check only matched raw `Struct` and tuple sources and waved through any aggregate cast to a wide-int target.

pairs.title: fix(gale): balance a rule-argument `[...]`, and expose a grammar's capture vocabulary

verdict.defect: The action stripper ended a parser rule's `[...]` argument list at the first `]`, so a `[]` host type such as `int[]` exposed the rest of the argument list (e.g. a `{1, 2}` initializer) to top-level action stripping.
verdict.reason: The culprit's original `[` handling tracked bracket depth, so it balanced `r[int[] arr]` correctly. The non-nesting `scan_char_class` behaviour came from a later change. The fix also corrects a secondary culprit-era bug, where a comment ending in `tokens` before `{` made the action read as a prequel, but that is not the headline defect.

pairs.title: fix(wir): give each bulk array clone its own temporaries

verdict.defect: The culprit dropped the `yields_results` guard on the tail of `return_every_exit`. A tail `Nop` left by rewriting a sibling `value; Br` exit, or a trailing store, was then fed to `lifted`, which reports failure and falsely marks the block as not fully rewritten. Separately, bulk array clones of the same type shared per-type temporaries, so a nested clone in `len` clobbered the outer clone's `src`.
verdict.reason: The array-clone temporary collision predates the culprit, which only wrapped the existing per-type names in `unshadowed`. The tail-lift regression comes directly from the culprit replacing the guarded `yields_results(last)` rewrite with an unconditional `all_rewritten &= lifted(last)`. A reviewer could see that its own sibling-exit path leaves a `Nop` as the last instruction.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): land or refuse a whole-value write through a `&mut` to a variant place

verdict.defect: A whole-value write (`*p = v`) through a `&mut` to a variant field, element or reborrow went into a detached box and never reached the place, so it was silently lost.
verdict.reason: The culprit only added confinement analysis and receiver-ref capture for value-copy elision; the blamed lines are its `compute_confined_params` call and signature, which the fix merely reworks to share a call graph. The lost write comes from how boxing represents `&mut` to variant places, which the culprit's diff does not touch.

pairs.title: fix(optimizer): price a cast by what it emits, and walk value-position blocks

verdict.defect: The inline cost model charged one instruction for every cast, including same-Wasm-shape casts (char/u32/bool) that emit nothing. Separately, condition_implication never visited blocks in value position.
verdict.reason: Both changes improve optimization quality (a heuristic re-tuning and a missed-optimization walk); neither fixes a crash, a wrong result or other incorrect behaviour. The culprit only carried the pre-existing flat per-cast charge over into its new instruction-weighted model.

pairs.title: fix(lsp): keep the receiver's argument slot in path-form parameter hints

verdict.defect: Parameter-name hints for path-form method calls like `Scale::scaled(&p, 2, 3)` dropped the `self` parameter even though the receiver is passed as args[0], so every label shifted one argument to the left.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `hint_static_method_call_args` and the impl-method fallback in `callee_param_names`, both using `filter_non_self_param_names`, which removes the receiver slot for calls that do pass it positionally. A reviewer could see that the same self-filtered list was zipped against `args` for both the dot form and the path form.

pairs.title: fix(optimizer): use the receiver verdict alone for a call's receiver slot

verdict.defect: The loop heap-effect summary computed a call's receiver borrow as `arg.is_mut || (receiver_borrowed && i == 0)`, so a method declared `&mut self` still marked its receiver as borrowed even when the receiver-immutable verdict proved the callee never writes through it.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the OR that lets the declared `is_mut` override the new verdict, which is visible in its diff, but the result is only conservative: an optimization is missed, and no miscompile, crash or wrong output occurs, so this is a precision improvement rather than a correctness fix.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): point every options diagnostic at the key it names

verdict.defect: Kiln options validation diagnostics had no span, so the driver's re-validation of inline `raw_options` reported them at line 1 of the consuming file, and the inline path blamed the whole `use` clause instead of the offending key.
verdict.reason: The culprit wrote span-less diagnostics, but at that time attribute entries carried no key spans and its inline path already patched missing spans onto the `use` decl; the line-1 misplacement comes from later driver re-validation of inline `raw_options`, which is not in the culprit. Per-key precision was not achievable from the culprit's data model, so a reviewer could not have flagged it as a defect there.

pairs.title: fix(nir): a census that walks the body sees the value pool's extraction sources

verdict.defect: Whole-body and subtree censuses (local usage, address-taken, rebound lets, callee collection, purity/trap checks, etc.) walked only skeleton children, so they missed nodes that a promoted operand names as its extraction source and reached wrong conclusions about live code.
verdict.reason: The culprit only refactored hand-rolled `for_each_child` stack walks into the equivalent skeleton-only `for_each_node_under`/`find_in_nodes_under` helpers, so the blind spot to extraction sources predates it. The blamed lines are a behaviour-preserving move, not where the defect was introduced.

pairs.title: fix(ownership): a binding read through a reference field keeps its own copy

verdict.defect: The value-copy share rule matched writes to reads only by root local, so a binding read through a reference field (a borrowed path) could alias storage that a write at a different root later changed, and observe that write.
verdict.reason: The root-keyed check (`m.path.root != path.root || write_cannot_reach`) and `compute_ref_targets` ignoring borrowed paths were already in the code before #1956. The culprit only restructured that check onto liveness, keeping the same root comparison, so the unsound aliasing it fixes is not new there and is not evident from its diff.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): a global initializer is a body — templates expand in one, and its closures' captures move with it

verdict.defect: Template strings inside global initializers were never expanded, which crashed pattern lowering. Separately, merging initializers into one `$initialize_module` renumbered locals without shifting closure captures' `outer_index`, so a capture read another initializer's local and the module failed Wasm validation.
verdict.reason: The culprit is an extraction refactor that moved existing lowering code (including `renumber_locals_in_expr`) into new files rather than writing new logic. The main defect, template expansion skipping globals, lives in `template.rs`, which is not in the culprit's diff at all.

pairs.title: fix(cli): a dev `wado test` run starts with its results, not a panic

verdict.defect: In a dev build, `wado test`'s stdlib prewarm workers reached the stdlib before `install_dev_stdlib` ran, so each worker panicked, and `let _ = handle.await` silently swallowed those panics.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the prewarm (including the panic-discarding `let _ = handle.await`, which contradicts its own comment), but the panic itself comes from the later dev-stdlib install mechanism being called per-subcommand rather than before dispatch. That mechanism does not exist in the culprit's diff, so the main defect was neither introduced by nor visible in it.

pairs.title: fix(kiln): diagnose a duplicate public type name instead of asserting

verdict.defect: Kiln hit an assertion instead of emitting a diagnostic when a duplicate public type name occurred; the visible geas parts of the fix also add checks on declared graph outputs and extend the ONNX grammar.
verdict.reason: The titled crash is in Kiln's compiler, which culprit #2105 never touched. The lines blamed on the culprit are in the Gale-generated ONNX parser and the geas grammar, and the fix changes there are deliberate grammar extensions plus label renumbering (external data, attrs after inputs). The culprit had documented those as stated limits, so they are not the defect being fixed.

pairs.title: fix(elaborator): diagnose a bound naming no trait, wherever it is written

verdict.defect: Bounds naming something that is not a declared trait were only diagnosed in supertrait clauses; such bounds on generic functions, structs, variants, impls, methods, associated types and packs went unreported.
verdict.reason: The culprit added supertraits and correctly reported unknown supertraits. The missing checks for every other bound position predate it and lie outside its diff, and the fix only replaces the culprit's supertrait-specific check with a general walk.

pairs.title: fix(gale): parse open-ended and nested LR suffixes as the ANTLR4 jar does; test codegen by running the parser

verdict.defect: A self-reference nested in an LR suffix subrule was given a fixed `conflict_min` precedence floor whenever an LR operator could follow it, instead of ANTLR4's plain `e[0]`; separately, a suffix was routed to the ATN simulator only when its static first set was empty, so open-ended suffixes like `(w | A)` or `A? .` were mis-dispatched and parses diverged from the ANTLR4 jar.
verdict.reason: The culprit added both pieces of logic the fix removes: the follow-aware `stamp_op_follow`/`build_lr_suffix_element` floor (the ATN side previously asserted instead of building) and the empty-`suffix_first`-only ATN-class test. Its diff explicitly reasons that a floor keeps the list operand from stealing `'>>'`, a claim a reviewer who knows ANTLR4's `e[0]` semantics could challenge, as could the empty-first-set-only open-ended check.

pairs.title: fix(loam): hf2loam names a malformed header, and next_token asserts its input

verdict.defect: next_token accepted an empty list, too many ids or out-of-vocabulary ids, which yields a negative row index or out-of-range lookups, and hf2loam's readHeader read a length prefix and header without checking them against the buffer size.
verdict.reason: The culprit adds next_token in a new file with no input checks: `(ids.len() - 1) * vocab` with empty ids is plainly visible, and so is the unchecked header length. The missing readHeader checks predate the culprit (the old Buffer version had them too), but the unvalidated next_token is entirely the culprit's.

pairs.title: fix: closures have no Display, and a closure local used as a method receiver no longer traps

verdict.defect: ClosureSafetyAnalyzer kept a closure local specialised when it was the receiver of any method call, so non-Inspect methods (inherent or trait methods on fn types) got a `&$Closure_N` where they expected a canonical closure and trapped.
verdict.reason: The culprit only added the closure Display/DisplayAlt delegate impls and the shared format-trait table that the fix deletes, which is a language-semantics change rather than the bug. The faulty `in_callee_position = true` for every call receiver in ClosureSafetyAnalyzer is untouched by the culprit's diff.

pairs.title: fix(run-webgpu): make on_submitted_work_done wait without hanging, on wasi-webgpu-wasmtime 0.3.1

verdict.defect: The host's `on-submitted-work-done` from the wasi-webgpu-wasmtime crate awaited a wgpu callback without polling any device, so the guest's `.wait()` hung forever.
verdict.reason: The hang comes from upstream library code, not from lines the culprit wrote; the culprit's blamed lines only pin the dependency in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock. Nothing in those manifest lines would let a reviewer see the missing device poll.

pairs.title: fix(core:temporal)!: follow TC39 Temporal as the specification

verdict.defect: The culprit's Temporal model diverged from TC39 Temporal in observable ways: duration digit runs silently wrapped `i64` on overflow, fractions past nine digits were accepted, the epoch range was unchecked, HTTP-date weekday names were never validated, and default largest units and rounding semantics differed from the spec.
verdict.reason: Much of the fix PR is a spec-alignment redesign, but it also corrects concrete wrong behaviour, such as the wrapping in `read_duration_number`, unbounded instants and invalid duration components being accepted, all in code the culprit added. Several of these are plainly visible in the culprit diff, for example the unchecked `value * 10 + digit` loop and the ignored weekday.

pairs.title: fix(core:json)!: settle the points where JSON readers disagree, and state each one

verdict.defect: JSON-to-integer reads with a fraction or exponent went through f64, so they lost precision past 2^53, and i128/u128 rejected forms like `1e2`; float tokens past the type's range also read silently as infinity.
verdict.reason: The f64 detour for exponent/fraction integer tokens and the infinity clamp were already in the pre-culprit code (`parse_i64_from` via `f64::from_str`, `fpfmt_parse`, `eff_p > 350 → INFINITY`), and so was the broken i128 handling of exponents. The culprit reorganized these paths into `checked_int_f64` and `scanned_to_f64` without introducing the wrong behaviour, though the lossy detour is plainly readable in its diff.

pairs.title: fix(grog): hold decode, encode and schema checks to the protobuf spec

verdict.defect: The runtime Grog shipped in the culprit has several decode/encode bugs: `Reader::map` calls `KS::take(self)?.unwrap()` on the key, which panics when a closed-enum key is undeclared. Message sizes are summed in i32 and can overflow. An open enum's first value is never checked to be 0, and implicit presence is allowed on closed-enum and message fields.
verdict.reason: All of these lines were newly written in the culprit's runtime and emitter. A reviewer could have spotted the `.unwrap()` on a fallible `take`, which the code's own comment says returns `None` for an undeclared closed-enum number, along with the i32 size arithmetic and the missing schema checks.

pairs.title: fix(opt): keep a field read through a reference sound across calls that may write it

verdict.defect: Field reads and copy bindings through a reference were treated as stable across calls that could write the pointee via a global, another argument's `&mut`, or an opaque host call. The culprit's `write_hits` counted a call as hitting only `mut_escaped` locals, and its new heap-effect summaries gave opaque callees no writes to objects held elsewhere.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the new `Write::Call`/`write_hits` logic in condition_implication and the whole heap_effect module, where `Target::Opaque` records only argument effects and none held elsewhere; the fix extends exactly these. A reviewer could see that a call never invalidates a reference-typed root unless it is `mut_escaped`, and that an opaque callee is never treated as writing globals.

pairs.title: fix(marl): stop the formatter from rewriting paragraphs into other blocks

verdict.defect: The block parser let any list marker (e.g. a wrapped `2010) b`), link reference definition, type-7 HTML tag, or other block start interrupt an open paragraph, and blockquotes did not take lazy continuation lines, so the formatter rewrote paragraph text into lists, definitions or separate blocks.
verdict.reason: The culprit wrote parse_blocks to check try_ref_def_line, is_html_block_start and is_list_marker before falling back to paragraph text, with no regard for an open paragraph, and wrote parse_blockquote to stop at the first non-`>` line. A reviewer who knows CommonMark's paragraph-interruption rules could see from the diff that `para` is never consulted before those checks.

pairs.title: fix: an effect inside a generic newtype's argument reaches the effect check

verdict.defect: Effect parameters and rows inside a generic newtype's type arguments were never reached: `effect_params_in` skipped `Newtype` and `zip_rows` stripped newtypes to their base, so those effects escaped the effect check (a missed missing-effect diagnostic and bogus mismatches).
verdict.reason: The culprit added `zip_rows` and `effect_params_in`, which handle `GenericInstance`/`GenericResource` arguments but not a `Newtype`'s own `type_args` (`zip_rows` jumps to `representation_head`). A reviewer could spot the missing newtype case in those new walkers.

pairs.title: fix(compiler): a by-value argument keeps its copy wherever the call may write it

verdict.defect: A by-value argument passed to a confined parameter had its copy elided unless it aliased a `&mut` argument of the same call, so a later argument or the callee writing that storage by other routes (assignment, closure capture, a held `&mut`, a global, another reference) changed the value the callee read.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `arg_confined`, which skips the copy based only on `call_mut_roots` (the `&mut` parameters' alias roots) plus a coarse let/match union-find, replacing the unconditional copy. A reviewer could see that writes made by assignments or side effects inside later arguments, through closures, or through globals are never considered.

pairs.title: fix(globals)!: reject every global initializer cycle an execution may take

verdict.defect: Inferred dependencies (those reached through calls) were dropped whenever they would close a cycle, and modules that depended on each other were ordered arbitrarily, so real initializer cycles compiled and then trapped or misbehaved at run time.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the `depends_on` yield for via-call edges and the `ready.unwrap_or(0)` fallback in `sort_modules_by_dependency`, and both silently break genuine cycles. Its own comments state that such edges yield and that a stuck module is just taken, so a reviewer could see that a cycle whose edges all run through calls, or that crosses a module boundary, goes unreported.

pairs.title: fix: a deferred local whose reference a call may keep compiles to valid Wasm

verdict.defect: The in-place-assignment decision ignored program order: any reference to a local anywhere in the body made every assignment to it write in place, including the first assignment to a deferred `let x: T;` local, which then wrote into storage that did not exist yet and produced invalid Wasm.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `in_place_assigns` and `unanalyzed_in_place_assigns`, which decide from a whole-body set of borrowed locals (`held`/`pending_bounded`) with no check that a reference precedes the site; the fix adds `ReferencePoints` to require a reference before the assignment. That flow-insensitivity is plainly visible in the culprit's diff, though seeing it break deferred locals takes knowing how they lower.

pairs.title: fix(test): end the run by naming every failed test

verdict.defect: Streaming reporters did not list failed or unexpectedly passing TODO tests at the end of the run, and the existing compile/load recap printed before the coverage summary rather than last.
verdict.reason: The fix mainly adds new recap sections and a new on_recap hook, which is a feature rather than a correction; it only incidentally moves the recap after coverage and guards against a heartbeat race. The culprit only added the coverage-finish step after on_run_done; the failure recap, whose ordering the fix changes, came from other code, so the culprit introduced no defect the fix corrects.

pairs.title: fix(serve): a service reaches the host network, as run and test do

verdict.defect: `wado serve` built its WASI context without granting host network access, so service handlers could not create TCP/UDP sockets or resolve names, while `wado run` and `wado test` could.
verdict.reason: The prior code explicitly documented deny-all networking for long-running services as a deliberate choice, so the fix is a policy change rather than a bug correction. The culprit only split out the serve constructor; the network grant in `build` (and so the divergence) came in a later change, so it is not in the culprit's diff.

pairs.title: fix: T::method checks every argument against its settled parameter

verdict.defect: The new T::method argument check in the culprit skipped the receiver entirely and skipped every parameter mentioning any type param, including the caller's settled `T`/`Self` and turbofish-instantiated method params, so mismatched arguments reached codegen as invalid modules.
verdict.reason: The culprit added `typecheck_settled_args` over `args[receiver..]` with a blanket `contains_type_param` skip, and it checks the receiver against nothing. In this body `T` is settled, so both omissions are visible in that diff. The fix checks the receiver too, binds the method's slots, and skips only still-unbound method slots.

pairs.title: fix: assign a whole affine aggregate without trapping, and refuse a reference the assignment leaves stale

verdict.defect: The move checker's `clear_place` forgot a place's moves when an assignment refilled it, and treated assignment as never invalidating a reference, so a reference taken before an assignment that moved-then-refilled or replaced what it pointed into was still accepted as readable.
verdict.reason: The culprit added the dangling-reference tracking: `owner_gone` detects a stale reference only through `moved`, and the new `clear_place` erases those entries on assignment without marking the holders that referred into the old object. A reviewer could see that `r = &a; eat(a); a = ...; r.id` would pass; the codegen trap half of the fix (`translate.rs`) is not in the culprit's shown diff.
